rationale: The primary limiter is an unsupported three-sided commercial structure: separate SME subscriptions, distributor or auditor feed and resale rights, and mandatory human review all have to work at once, while established vendors already cover the core workflow. The single redesign collapses payer, permissioned data source, and distribution into one anchor relationship: an ingredient distributor buys a managed supplier-change intake and human-governed exception service for a permissioned portfolio and bundles access into its customer service; manufacturers remain workflow users and qualified approvers rather than separate subscribers. This changes the customer, payer and paid event, offer and business model, distribution mechanism, and compounding data context. It also removes the unsupported 300-site subscription path and makes expansion conditional on measured contribution and renewal of a small number of distributor contracts. Distributor willingness, rights, contract value, review burden, and renewal remain unvalidated, so the redesign is a lawful testable structure rather than a claim of traction.
